claims.statement: The retired Fleet pilot account rodman.mac@stuhlmuller.net remains separate from the owner and has no Fleet console or Platform SSO assignment; its operator module requires a managed domain and cannot plan against current Google federation.

Fleet-only Company Portal and Platform SSO are retired. The separate owner conversion is blocked by current Google federation; any later attempt needs a reviewed managed target, recovery administrator, preparation receipt, and attestation.

The October 7, 2026 Octelium migration bound the original owner oid with email fallback disabled and verified owner sessions before and after the mail change; the old SMTP alias remained reserved. Fleet-only Platform SSO was subsequently retired.

The operator-only Tailscale provider owns full policy adoption and three distinct-tag reusable, ephemeral, preauthorized CI auth keys with 90-day expiry and explicit committed rotation generations; existing unused federated identities remain protected until final migration retirement.
Tailscale CI plan receives read access and dry-run Application writes guarded by fail-closed admission; the apply tag receives cluster administration.

The fixed CI publisher verifies and caches the distinct credential authority before publishing three fixed secrets; old client-ID variables are removed only after all writes and metadata checks. Retirement preview and execution validate every cached current signature and all previous authority metadata before any removal, retaining per-target rechecks and safe already-absent retries; preview never signs, publishes or changes cache contents.
The trusted Mac publisher passes raw CI auth keys to Tailscale lock sign through file:/dev/stdin, avoiding raw-key arguments and temporary files that the sandboxed macOS app cannot read.

Phase 2a retains Tunnel and Octelium credentials until separate acceptance. The tailnet resolver needs no DNS write token and serves 29 current approved names; feature 005 limits guarded public A/AAAA/CNAME deletion to the fixed 26 non-apex migration names after client acceptance, preserving the public apex and DNS-01.

The CI publisher durably stores a private pending wrapped-key receipt before post-sign readback, polls for exactly one matching new authority without prior trust drift, and resumes the same receipt after timeout before signing further keys.

Separate orphan recovery requires an exact current-provider authority, matching Mac and recent creation metadata, no pending or matching cache and no fixed published secrets, and an empty read-only affected-signature query before removing only that authority without re-signing or publication.

The active Harbor Kustomization stages namespace-local harbor-pull Docker credentials from the existing Harbor read-only robot parameter. The vulnerability exporter uses them only for kubelet image pulls; the held private-core candidate uses the same prerequisite. No new SSM parameter or IAM grant is added. Native-image activation waits for publication/scans, recovery clearance, and ExternalSecret readiness; OnChange rotation requires a declared annotation advance and upstream cold recovery remains.

The reviewed Stage A saved plan created and metadata-verified `/homelab/harbor/mirror-robot-pull-password` without exposing its value. Stage B declares `harbor-secrets` revision `v4` and mounts the reader key in the Harbor bootstrap Job; after External Secrets materializes the target Secret, that Job can reconcile the separate reader robot during execution, while successful PostSync is required before acceptance. Its operator materializer verifies reviewed `main` before and after a private SSM read and writes fixed reader-auth JSON outside the checkout with owner-only permissions. An ordinary executable Talos mirror rollout requires supplied reader auth unless the captured configuration already contains valid `robot$mirror+pull` auth; otherwise it stops before candidate or apply. Rollback and `--registry-host-only` execution intentionally do not use reader auth. The public mirror remains public until a separate reviewed private-pull acceptance.

Mastodon declares ten exact SSM parameters, generating internal keys in encrypted state while the protected SMTP workflow writes only its fixed external credential slot; file-mounted OnChange consumers require declared refresh and runtime revisions after rotation.

Fleet-managed Mac Google login stages an operator-only /homelab/fleet/google-oauth SecureString outside External Secrets. The XCreds operator privately reads the OAuth client and delivers a host-scoped MDM profile only after protected merge and deployment. The pilot requires email-claim mapping, local login fallback and FileVault acceptance; remote profile removal requires verified native login and explicit operator attestation.

The native Harbor scan robot requires /homelab/harbor/robot-scan-password and its exact-ARN External Secrets reader grant. Read-only SSM metadata and IAM inspection on 2026-10-18 verified the version 1 SecureString and grant, and a targeted plan from main at f6506136 found no changes. The parameter alone creates no Harbor robot or receipt.

The staged Cordium runner controller uses a separate namespace and ExternalSecret for its GitHub App key and Cordium auth token; registration and controller deployment stay disabled pending identity, isolation, publication, and cold-pull acceptance.

Fleet, Grafana and Octelium bind the existing Entra owner by immutable object ID. The read-only conversion helper rejects the current federated target, so conversion needs a separate reviewed federation or target-domain change before preparation.
The retired owner-mail Terraform unit uses a removed block with destroy=false to forget its Graph PATCH state after review, without another mail write or alias-release attempt.
Post-conversion attestation requires clearing the recovery Azure CLI session and signing in as the converted owner; the helper validates the Graph caller's immutable ID and target UPN.

The Renovate App SecureStrings reached version 2 and refreshed the automation/renovate ExternalSecret; the temporary writer role was removed after a reviewed plan. The ExternalSecret projects the credentials as files, and the hourly UTC CronJob remains in full dry-run mode while the legacy Action is the only writer. The App lacks repository Administration read, so its first write-enabled outcome needs policy review.

OpenClaw Enterprise declares a distinct SSM model API key and protected fixed-target writer for an owner-supplied OpenRouter key; the selected OpenAI-compatible model is openrouter/free, activation remains disabled until consumer refresh and real inference pass, and no stopped legacy OpenClaw or LiteLLM credential is imported.

The unregistered Enterprise foundation declares restricted system and agent namespaces, exact OnChange SSM projections with retained targets, and a still-placeholder dedicated model key; this source does not prove secret readiness or activate an agent.

The dormant Enterprise database Secret templates separate application and migration URLs using verify-full TLS against a retained cert-manager PostgreSQL CA and private Service certificate; PostgreSQL consumers and live TLS acceptance remain pending.

The dormant Enterprise application binds reviewed non-secret Installation bytes by SHA-256 to a versioned immutable startup Secret; its protected exact-main path only creates or verifies that fixed Secret after the foundation namespace exists.

The startup Secret initially omits the Installation ID; the protected binder attests the returned ID and stable Ready controllers, then guards and verifies its annotation patch, while live binding remains pending.

The Multica runtime bootstraps a 90-day personal token on first use, retains it on its private profile volume, and relies on the pinned daemon to renew the same token when seven days or less remain; a stored revoked or expired token is not silently replaced.

The 19:00 and 20:00 scheduled Renovate dry runs hit the same public canary datasource key on separate cache-PVC Pods; after protected v0.0.2 publication, the 21:00 run refreshed that record and selected a new public canary branch proposal, completing T022.

The fixed platform credential helper requires an exact clean main checkout and verifies the Octelium WORKLOAD user, CLIENT-only policy, and private TCP Talos service before creating or rotating a dedicated 30-day AUTH_TOKEN Credential. It publishes only OCE_OCTELIUM_CLIENT_AUTH_TOKEN in homelab-production and does not delete the user's separate clientless sessions.

The platform credential helper issues a distinct 30-day Talos os:admin client from a valid operator client, verifies different certificate and key plus read-only Talos access, then publishes only the encoded new client as OCE_TALOSCONFIG_B64 in homelab-production.

Protected platform inspect run 39362087271 stopped at connect_talos because the dedicated Octelium CLIENT and Talos configuration inputs were empty; the repository helper had only local tests, so live issuance, tunnel access, and complete inspection receipt remain unverified.

The dormant firewall cleanup lane stores capture, approval, attempt and completion evidence in a private versioned bucket; a fresh protected owner approval verifies the reviewed digest, live snapshot, absent fixture namespace and workloads, exact reviewed canary Pod inventory and current main before writing an immutable capture-run-specific receipt, and partial deletion requires fresh review.

The source-only protected Enterprise binding lane rechecks exact current main and pins the reviewed Installation binder, but its hosted runner has no declared delivery for the owner-controlled 0600 bootstrap service-key file; no live binding has occurred.

The staged Enterprise journal operator uses a dedicated service account without automatic token mounting; its one-shot Job projects a short-lived token and CA, and its read-only RBAC grants GET on only the exact reviewed Installation Secret.

The operator bundle is not registered in active GitOps and its gate stays disabled until the UID-10001-owned 0600 bootstrap key file and other activation prerequisites are proved, so its declared permissions are not live access.

The fixed protected Talos and Kubernetes upgrade stages consume private role-specific control-plane and worker configs, but the committed activation gate is false and required placement, recovery, and publication receipts have not passed.
